title: Microcredit capacity: HC prioritization & price-coverage playbook
content:
Executive summary:

Small working playbook to decide near-term hires and capacity-credit allocation tied to a microcredit product we may pilot for small customers (token-backed credits for low-volume teams). Purpose is to map out headcount prioritization, runway impact, and pricing sensitivity triggers. This is a living sheet — assumptions below are intentionally conservative.

Key decision questions:
- When do we convert microcredit pilot into persistent slab / reserved offering? (trigger = sustained utilization > 60% of allocated microcredit capacity for 8 weeks)
- Which hires (infra vs sales vs CS) materially improve unit economics for microcredit?
- How much price floor/ceiling to set for early adopters to protect margin while testing elasticity?

Assumptions (working):
- Time horizon: 6 months (Jun 2026 — Nov 2026).
- Microcredit unit: 1 microcredit = 100k tokens. Pricing tested in $ per 100k-token buckets.
- Cost per 100k tokens on hosted fleet (avg, incl infra amortization & GPU ops) = $0.95 (base) under current utilization; quantization savings not yet applied.
- Contribution margin target for pilot = 30% (before S&M allocation).
- Elasticity model: each 10% price decrease -> +7% demand (short-run), each 10% price increase -> -5% demand. (calibrated from early telemetry, highly uncertain)
- HC ramp assumptions: average hire lead time = 6 weeks, ramp productivity = linear over 10 weeks.

Scenario matrix (revenue vs demand sensitivity):
- Base: price = $1.25 / 100k tokens, demand uplift from marketing = +0% -> monthly microcredit sold = 48k units (initial pilot small); gross margin = (price - cost)/price = (1.25-0.95)/1.25 = 24% (below target).
- Price floor test: price = $1.05 -> expected demand +6% -> gross margin = (1.05-0.95)/1.05 = 9.5% (worse).
- Price premium: price = $1.45 -> expected demand -5% -> gross margin = (1.45-0.95)/1.45 = 34.5% (meets target) but risk of lower adoption.
- Upside (quantization + batching gains): effective cost drops to $0.70 -> at price $1.25 margin = 44%.

Headcount plan (prioritized hires — short list):
- 1 Senior SRE (infra ops, focus on capacity packing & batching) — ETA onboard: 2026-07-15, fully ramped by 2026-09-01, loaded cost/month = $24,000. Rationale: directly reduces cost per token via autoscaling/packing.
- 1 ML Infra Engineer (inference kernels / quantization/test harness) — ETA onboard: 2026-08-01, cost/month = $20,000. Rationale: potential quantization projects that could drop cost by $0.15-0.30/100k tokens.
- 0.5 Customer Success (fractional from pool) — starts immediately (part-time contractor) cost/month = $6,500. Rationale: convert pilots, increase ARPA.
- 1 Growth / GTM PM (pilot ops + pricing experiments) — ETA onboard: 2026-06-25, cost/month = $14,000. Rationale: run A/B pricing and tracking.

Quick headcount cost table (monthly impact):
- Current baseline monthly run-rate for product line (ops + shared allocations): $220,000
- +Senior SRE: +24,000 -> new run-rate = $244,000
- +ML Infra Eng: +20,000 -> new run-rate = $264,000
- +0.5 CS: +6,500 -> new run-rate = $270,500
- +GTM PM: +14,000 -> new run-rate = $284,500

Projected token throughput and unit economics (month 3 and month 6 snapshots):
- Month 3 (Sep 2026) — with hires: microcredit units sold/month = 52k, total tokens = 5.2B, revenue @ $1.25 = $65,000, cost @ $0.95 = $49,400, gross margin = 24% -> but after incremental HC (~$58k/mo across hires when annualized vs only microcredit revenue) negative contribution.
- Month 6 (Nov 2026) — if quantization success, cost -> $0.75: revenue @ $1.25 on 60k units = $75,000, cost = $45,000, gross margin 40%, incremental HC absorbed across portfolio -> net positive on pilot.

Pricing sensitivity quick matrix (illustrative):
- Price / 100k | Demand delta | Revenue | Cost (per 100k) | Gross margin
- 0.95         | +10%         | 52.8k*0.95 | 0.95            | 0%
- 1.05         | +6%          | 50.9k*1.05 | 0.95            | 9.5%
- 1.25 (base)  | 0%           | 48k*1.25   | 0.95            | 24%
- 1.45         | -5%          | 45.6k*1.45 | 0.95            | 34.5%
Notes: demand numbers are approximate pilot unit counts; use absolute units for monthly sold in downstream models.

Trigger rules (operational):
- Hire SRE (greenlight) if: 4-week rolling utilization of microcredit capacity > 55% and projected 12-week token backlog > 2x current capacity.
- Start ML quantization sprint (hire or contractor) if: average cost per 100k > $0.90 for 6 weeks AND sales conversion < 12% on trial.
- Increase price by $0.20 if: 6-week A/B shows no significant drop in churn and price elasticity in A group < 0.08 (i.e., demand elasticity low).
- Apply introductory credit (10% discount) if: pilot sign-ups fall below target by >20% versus forecast for 3 consecutive weeks.

Runway & sensitivity (high-level):
- Current committed budget for product pilot headcount bucket = $400k (6 months).
- If we hire full prioritized list, incremental burn = ~$348k over 6 months (simple sum of loaded cost * months). Runway impact = consumes ~87% of pilot headcount bucket.
- Sensitivity: a -10% price shock without cost improvement -> additional monthly deficit ~ $4k-6k; a successful quantization -> monthly improvement ~$8k-14k.

Open questions / unknowns (notes to CFO & Head of Product):
- How much of the SRE/ML infra hires are generalizable across product lines? We should apportion cost instead of charging pilot 100% if cross-customer benefit exists. Need consensus on allocation method (pro-rata by token usage or by feature-owner).
- Should we set up a small on-call incentive for quantization experiments (to accelerate kernel integration)? Cost vs speed tradeoff.
- Do we allow pilot customers to receive volume refunds if token cost falls post-quantization? (legal + sales implications).

Action items (next 4 weeks):
- Priya to run two-arm pricing A/B with control ($1.25) vs high ($1.45) on a 20% sample. Metric: conversion to paid within 14 days, churn in 30 days. (JIRA: JIRA-FIN-987)
- Ethan to scope a 6-week quantization quick-win project and provide expected delta (conservative/likely/upside). Deliverable: engineering KPI doc by 2026-06-20.
- Maya (owner) to draft allocation proposal for cross-product HC cost sharing; send to finance leadership by 2026-06-10.

Appendix: quick sensitivity calculation notes (for modeling team)
- Use baseline demand D0 = 48,000 microcredit units/month. Price elasticity e approximated as: pct_change_demand = -0.6 * pct_change_price (short-run). Calibrate with observed pilot telemetry (attached in linked artifacts).
- Contribution per unit = price - cost - incremental HC allocation (if applicable). For modeling, assume incremental HC allocation = full loaded hire cost divided by expected microcredit-attributable months (best practice: apportion 30% of SRE cost to this product line if shared).

References & links:
- Pilot metrics dashboard (internal): CONFLUENCE-PRICING-8842
- Experiment plan (JIRA): JIRA-FIN-987
- Early quantization spec PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pricing-playbook/pull/42

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally light on final numbers; it should seed the budget workbook (Finance will ingest numbers into the master Q3/Q4 workbook). Tagging as draft because we will iterate after A/B results and quantization scoping.
